data.title: Why Is CRWV Stock Rising Overnight?
data.description:
Key points:
  • CoreWeave faces concerns over its high debt levels.
  • Last week, CoreWeave reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its sales and operating profit forecasts for 2026
  • Retail sentiment for CRWV notched up but remained in the ‘bearish’ zone.

One of CoreWeave’s co-founders announced Wednesday purchasing a major lot of the company’s bonds, boosting sentiment for the stock that has faced persistent weakness in recent months.

“Last week, I purchased $30 million in face value of CoreWeave’s unsecured bonds. I intend to hold them to maturity on October 1, 2031,” CoreWeave’s Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo said in a LinkedIn post.

“When we started CoreWeave, I couldn’t have imagined the scale of what our customers are building with us today... I’ve never been more confident in CoreWeave,” he wrote.

CRWV stock rose 0.6% in overnight trading late in the day, after falling 4.1% in the regular session.

CoreWeave has faced investor concerns over its high debt levels. Some investors believe those risks have increased of late, amid growing concerns that cloud computing capacity could eventually outstrip demand and that a Democrat-led government could slow data center construction. CRWV suffered a sharp fall last month and the stock is now down 33.2% year to date.

CoreWeave’s Strong Results Fail To Keep Stock Afloat

Last week, CoreWeave reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its sales and operating profit forecasts for 2026. That led to a 25% post-earnings rally on Nov. 11, but the pump faded in the following days.

CoreWeave revenue backlog rose 138% year-over-year to about $132.5 billion, but its debt also climbed at a rapid clip to support the buildout of new data centers.

Total debt rose from roughly $21 billion at the end of 2025 to $35.6 billion in Q2 2026 and about $66.22 billion in Q3 2026.

Peers Nebius (NBIS) and Iren Ltd. (IREN) also reported strong results for the last quarter, but delays in some of their capacity coming online dampened the investor view.

Citi analysts named CoreWeave as one of their top picks, arguing that recent earnings reports reinforced a preference for data and AI infrastructure names, and that neoclouds moved up in its rankings amid "signs of strong AI demand and nicer valuations."

CoreWeave’s co-founders, including Venturo, have sold a combined $3.3 billion in shares since the company’s March 2025 initial public offering, including $2.4 billion this year.

Retail View On CRWV

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for CRWV improved but remained in the ‘bearish’ zone.

“$CRWV Last shakeout, now we get the chasing time. As uncomfortably far down as it went, will now do the opposite,” a trader said.

Another trader, with a contrarian view, wrote: “$CRWV even if AI works, the ECB warns the credit boom could leave overcapacity and credit losses. Seems like CoreWeave is built for full utilization, not for leftovers.”

data.title: Dan Ives Says Nvidia’s AI Dominance Can Survive Without Jensen Huang: ‘Two, Three Years Ahead’ Of Rivals
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dan Ives called Jensen Huang one of the U.S.’ most important technology leaders.
  • According to Ives, Huang's exit and ongoing investigations have left investors uncertain.
  • Ives remains bullish on Nvidia, saying its chip technology is two to three years ahead of rivals and China.

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) could remain an artificial intelligence powerhouse even without Jensen Huang, according to tech analyst Dan Ives, who sees the chipmaker as critical to U.S. economic future. He added that Nvidia’s AI dominance was bigger than one executive and its chip technology was two to three years ahead of its competitors.

Calling Nvidia the “central nervous system” of the U.S. economy, Ives highlighted its central role in AI and capital spending.

Nvidia stock edged 0.3% higher overnight Wednesday. The stock is down 7.3% so far this week and is on track for a seventh straight week in the red.

Why Huang's Leadership Matters For Nvidia 

Speaking with Phil Rosen on the Full Signal podcast, Ives, a partner at Yorkville, described Huang as one of U.S.’ most strategically important technology figures, pointing to Nvidia’s central role in the global semiconductor industry and the competition between Washington and Beijing.

“Jensen’s the most important technology asset in the United States. Now you could hate him, love him, that’s just factual, that’s the reality. Then it’s like the biggest gating factor between China and the U.S. is Nvidia and Jensen.”

He added that Huang's exit creates a difficult situation for investors. The board must decide whether he can remain CEO as investigations and China-related allegations continue. Ives said the probes could last several months, keeping questions about the company's leadership unresolved.

“No doubt, Nvidia is different without Jensen. There’s no way to sugarcoat that.”

Nvidia’s AI Chip Dominance Could Outlast Jensen Huang

Despite the leadership questions, Ives remains optimistic about Nvidia’s competitive position. He argued that the company has a technological advantage of roughly two to three years over rival chipmakers.

“Without Jensen, let’s just say Jensen sails into the sunset and has his own chip company, goes with Musk to SpaceX, wherever it may be. We’re still bullish on Nvidia because the reality is they’re two, three years ahead of any competitor, chip-wise. They’re two, three years ahead of China and they’re the one chip in the world fueling the AI revolution.”

Ives said the Nvidia leadership turmoil has made this one of the most unusual weeks of his 27-year career and added that the company’s importance to AI and U.S. business investment makes the situation even more significant.

“Nvidia’s the central nervous system, not just of AI, but, I would say of the U.S. economy relative to CapEx.”

In its first earnings report since parting ways with Jensen Huang last week, the chip giant posted fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-on-year and above analysts' estimate of $109.3 billion, as per Fiscal.ai.

 NVDA Stock: Retail View 

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

A user said, “$NVDA cheaper shares than $AMD just saying.”

Another user said, “Open question for Nvidia’s board: If Nvidia's financial performance is so extraordinary, and the person principally responsible for building that business has publicly expressed willingness to return, what precisely is the board's rationale for categorically excluding him?”

NVDA stock has declined 19% year-to-date.

data.title: Asian stocks fail to get a lift from Anthropic's IPO pricing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic blockbuster IPO pricing fails to lift Asian stocks
  • US stock futures gain in anticipation of the biggest-ever IPO
  • Investor worries over AI trade cast shadow
  • Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to 19-month high

By Ankur Banerjee

Asian stocks slid on Thursday as fears over the AI trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials left sentiment fragile ahead of an eagerly awaited market debut from Anthropic after the Claude chatbot maker scored the biggest IPO ever.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about $1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing.

"I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI," he said. "I think much of that boils down to future investment growth."

Traders' immediate reaction was to push US stock futures higher, with Nasdaq futures up nearly 1% and S&P futures 0.6% higher.

Asian equities, though, fell sharply, led by the three top chipmakers: TSMC , Samsung and SK Hynix were all down 2%. That left South Korea's KOSPI down 1% while Taiwanese stocks TWSE:TAIEX slid 3.8%.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) slumped 1.9%, hitting a seven-month low. The index was set for a decline of nearly 6% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since early March.

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken over the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build related infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, said the Anthropic IPO is a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won’t settle the debate," she said. "There’s a genuine wall of worry right now, and it’ll take a few things to climb it."

DOLLAR FIRMS ON HAWKISH FED

In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of a rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0978, hovering near its lowest point since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 157.42 per US dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against six other currencies, was 0.1% higher at 103.92, a 19-month high.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

The comments followed hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, leaving markets to brace for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD."

The Australian dollar slipped 0.75% to a 10-month low after soft jobs data cemented the view that Australian rates have likely peaked.

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were 0.58% lower at $91.47 a barrel, set for a third straight weekly decline.

data.title: Jade Gas Completes Mongolia’s First Multi-Lateral CBM Well Ahead of Planned HKEX Listing
data.description:
Jade Gas Holdings has drilled and completed Mongolia’s first multi-lateral coal bed methane well at Red Lake, within its flagship Tavan Tolgoi coal bed methane project (TTCBM) project.

The well comprises a main wellbore and four lateral branches targeting Seam IIIb, the same coal seam intersected by Red Lake’s two existing single-lateral production wells.

It has a combined 2,642 metres of in-seam drilling, representing approximately 93% of across the horizontal sections and a significant increase in reservoir contact compared with either of the existing wells.

China-based contractor Yan’an Drilling Wellking Energy Technical Service completed activities ahead of the original end-November target, demonstrating efficient execution of the multi-lateral drilling and completion design.

The design increases contact with gas-bearing coal from a single wellbore, allowing it to potentially expand a well’s drainage area, improve gas recovery, and achieve higher flow rates.

Co-Ordinated Dewatering

Jade is now preparing for co-ordinated dewatering of the new well with the existing wells to assess the potential benefits of a multi-lateral design under Red Lake reservoir conditions.

The work is expected to start before month end following completion of surface preparations including installation of a progressive cavity pump (PCP) and wellhead motor in the new well and trenching for the water and gas pipelines.

Combined monitoring of all wells will help Jade assess reservoir pressure responses and optimise dewatering practices, while water production, pressure, and gas flow data will guide operational adjustments.

The new well’s gas production capability will be assessed as dewatering progresses, with drilling results and subsequent production testing to improve well design, completion practices, and operational planning for a development drilling campaign in the new year.

The Red Lake field sits in the Tavan Tolgoi Basin, which has high demand for electricity, fuel, and the base load energy supply necessary to underpin the region’s intermittent renewables.

Hong Kong Listing

Jade has signed a binding mandate appointing a Tier 1 Hong Kong investment bank as a sponsor for its planned listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEX).

The sponsor’s investment banking group has previously assisted more than 500 mainland Chinese companies to list on the HKEX using its experience in cross-border equity offerings, energy sector financing, and global commodities.

Jade will work with the sponsor and its advisers on due diligence and preparation of a listing application and will present its investment case to a broader audience, including investors with a focus on the energy sector.

A Hong Kong listing offers the company an additional platform to engage with institutional investors and potential strategic partners, broadening its shareholder base, improving access to Asian capital markets, and supporting greater trading liquidity as it advances the TTCBM project.

data.title: Jio Financial and BlackRock inject capital into India venture
data.description:
Jio Financial Services (BSE : 543940) and BlackRock (NYSE : BLK) have each put INR1.23bn ($13.16mn) into Jio BlackRock Asset Management, their equally owned joint venture, the Indian company said in a stock exchange filing on November 18.

The joint venture will use the money to fund its business operations. The capital came through a rights issue. Each partner subscribed to 123mn equity shares with a face value of INR10 apiece, and the shares were allotted at par for cash on the day of the filing. The disclosure follows an earlier filing on the venture dated December 10, 2025.

Jio Financial Services classified the transaction as a related party deal and said it was carried out on an arm's length basis. According to the filing, none of the company's promoters, promoter group entities or other group companies has any interest in the investment. The company said the deal needs no approval from any government body or regulator. Its payment went through at 1:58pm.

Mohana V, the Group Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of Jio Financial Services, signed the filing, which the company submitted to Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's listing and disclosure rules.

data.title: Big Caring Shares Log Gains After Opening Below IPO Price
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Big Caring is reversing its weak start on Bursa Malaysia following Malaysia's second-largest initial public offering.

Shares of Malaysia's largest pharmacy chain rose by as much as 10% after opening at 1.05 ringgit on Thursday, below the IPO price of 1.08 ringgit. The shares were recently 7.4% higher than the IPO price at 1.16 ringgit each.

The company raised about 2.03 billion ringgit, equivalent to $493.3 million, through the sale of about 1.9 billion shares. The IPO was 4.31 times oversubscribed.

The deal was backed by 19 cornerstone investors, including abrdn Malaysia, AHAM Asset Management and Eastspring Investments.

Big Caring, Malaysia's largest pharmacy retailer by revenue and number of licensed pharmacies, operates more than 650 pharmacies in the country. It plans to use the proceeds from its IPO to repay loans, establish a new distribution center and covering listing expenses.

The company plans to open 40 to 50 new outlets annually over the next three to five years.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported on the pharmacy chain's plan to go public this year.

MBSB Research initiated coverage on Big Caring with a 1.20 ringgit target price.

The research house expects the company's core earnings to grow 37.3% in fiscal 2027, driven by outlet expansion, sustained same-store sales growth and interest savings from its plan to repay debt.

It said Big Caring deserves a valuation premium to its peers given the company's vertically integrated business model and leading position in Malaysia's pharmacy retail market.

Deal activity in Malaysia's healthcare sector has been strong in recent quarters, fueled by rising patient volumes and healthcare spending.

In the first nine months of 2026, 47 companies raised a combined $1.49 billion in Malaysia's capital market. Sunway Healthcare's IPO of more than $700 million is the largest so far this year.

data.title: Hong Kong drops case against Chinese sea captain over Baltic pipeline damage
data.description:
Hong Kong has dropped its prosecution of the Chinese captain of a Hong Kong-registered container ship Newnew Polar Bear accused of severing a Baltic Sea gas pipeline in October 2023, media said on Wednesday.

  • Prosecution lawyers told a magistrate's court several witnesses from the Chinese mainland could not be contacted, media said.

  • Captain Wan Wenguo, who is in his 40s, is expected to be deported to mainland China after being held in custody since December 2024, the South China Morning Post newspaper said.

  • A lawyer for Wan, Jerry Chung, had said 18 prosecution witnesses would be called to testify.

  • Wan pleaded not guilty to a charge of criminally damaging a section of the 77-km (48-mile) Balticconnector natural gas pipeline between Estonia and Finland, but guilty to two lesser charges of falling short of safety compliance

  • Finnish investigators have said the vessel dragged its anchor to sever the pipeline, while tests showed a broken anchor retrieved from the seabed nearby belonged to the vessel, which was missing an anchor

  • China had promised both Finland and Estonia to assist with the investigations and called for an objective and fair probe

data.title: MSTR Stock Recovers Overnight After Dip – But Analyst Downgrades Strategy To 'Sell' As Bitcoin Premium Faces Pressure
data.description:
Key points:
  • Monness Crespi said its Sell rating is a call on BTC, the company's leverage, and the stock's premium to BTC holdings. 
  • BTC prices fell below $63,000 amid a selloff as inflation concerns and the Federal Reserve’s hawkish comments weighed further on the already pressured digital asset.
  • A recent regulatory filing revealed that Strategy bought back 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million between Nov. 9 and 15, leaving $332.2 million under its preferred stock repurchase program.

Shares of Strategy (MSTR) reversed to the green in the overnight session after closing more than 6% lower on Wednesday amid persistent weakness in Bitcoin (BTC) prices.

BTC prices fell below $63,000 amid a selloff as inflation concerns and the Federal Reserve’s hawkish comments weighed on the already-pressured digital asset.

Monness Crespi downgraded Strategy to ‘Sell’ from ‘Neutral’ with a $65 price target, implying a downside of about 28% from the stock’s last close.

Analyst Cites Weakness In Bitcoin For MSTR Downgrade

Monness Crespi said its Sell rating is a call on BTC, the company's leverage, and the stock's premium to BTC holdings.

The firm noted that Bitcoin ETF outflows continue, options pricing shows demand for downside protection, and prediction markets imply substantial downside risk for the cryptocurrency. The firm added that it believes the premium investors pay for Bitcoin per share growth will decline as equity dilution is increasingly used to fund STRC repurchases and preferred dividends.

Strategy’s Growing Buybacks

A recent regulatory filing revealed that Strategy bought back 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million between Nov. 9 and 15, leaving $332.2 million under its preferred stock repurchase program. At that pace, it covers about 10 days.

Most of Strategy’s money came from selling its common stock for $244.7 million last week. Of that, $206.3 million was allocated to STRC repurchases. The buyback was nearly seven times as large as Strategy's Bitcoin purchase that week.

MSTR Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR stock dipped from ‘neutral’ to ‘bearish’ over 24 hours amid ‘high’ message volumes.

One user said, “$MSTR Only an idiot would buy a stock that's diluted by 2 million shares every freaking week! Should be illegal.”

Another user said, “$MSTR Company with no revenue how the F sailor find money to buy bitcoin? You know the rest, endless dilution endless dumping.”

MSTR stock is down more than 40% in 2026.

data.title: Aluminium, copper prices fall up to 21%, but auto companies’ margin relief expected in Q4
data.description:
Falling metal prices should help carmakers' profits, but the relief will not come straight away. Steel is the exception, as its prices are still rising.

The benefit is unlikely to be immediate because of the procurement cycle. About 75% of a quarter's procurement costs reflect the previous quarter's commodity prices.

The gains from cheaper commodities are therefore expected to show up more in Q4 than in Q3 FY27.

Several commodities have corrected sharply:

  • Copper is at a seven-month low and has turned flat for 2026.
  • Aluminium is at a 51-week low.
  • Silver is at a 14-month low.
  • Gold is at a 12-month low.
  • Tin is at an eight-month low.

From their recent peaks, prices have fallen as follows:

CommodityRecent peak (₹/kg)Latest price (₹/kg)Fall
Copper₹1,432₹1,21515%
Aluminium₹397₹31321%
Zinc₹452₹39413%

Steel Defies Trend

Domestic steel prices averaged ₹63,965 per tonne in October-November. That is 7% higher than the Q2 FY27 average of ₹59,800 per tonne.

Margins Under Fire

Auto makers (OEMs) saw revenue rise 29.4% year-on-year (YoY) in Q2, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 19%. Margins came under pressure across segments, falling by up to 400 basis points (bps).

Aluminium, copper, rubber, and plastic components account for 40-45% of passenger vehicle (PV) raw material (RM) costs.

Commodity costs hit individual companies as follows:

  • Tata Motors PV: The impact was 4% of revenue in Q1 and a further 3% in Q2.
  • Bajaj Auto: The impact was 4.5% of revenue in Q1 and a further 3.5% in Q2.
  • Hyundai: Margins fell 400 bps YoY and 250 bps quarter-on-quarter (QoQ).
  • Maruti Suzuki: The material cost ratio rose 420 bps.
  • Escorts Kubota: The EBITDA margin fell 401 bps.

data.title: Anthropic IPO: Here are the early backers whose investments are now worth billions
data.description:
Anthropic PBC's record-breaking IPO is set to bring in returns worth billions of dollars for several financial firms that bet the house on the Claude chatbox maker. The company, after its debut on Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, will be the first-ever frontier lab to go public. It priced its shares at $83 apiece, giving it an approximately $1.5 trillion valuation, up around $100 billion from the higher end of its previous range. Bloomberg has compiled a list of some of the largest and notable financial investors in Anthropic that stand to gain from the IPO. Here's what the report reveals:

Iconiq | A wealth management company turned Silicon Valley private markets investor has put in over $6 billion in Anthropic. It has previously backed OpenAI and it wrote its first check to Anthropic last year, when the company was valued at $183 billion, which is now just a fraction of its IPO price. Iconiq's $6 billion bet is its largest private investment ever. Based on its pre-IPO investments, Its stake in Anthropic would be worth more than $26 billion at the firm's $1.5 trillion IPO valuation.

Spark Capital | The only venture capitalist listed as a board member in Anthropic's filing is Yasmin Razavi, a general partner at Spark Capital and an early backer of the firm. Spark Capital put in $75 million in Anthropic in 2023. At its current valuation, Spark Capital's stake would be worth around $11 billion..

Menlo Ventures | It was one of the first venture companies to invest in Anthropic in 2023. In the following year, it led the Claude chatbox maker's Series D round with a check of $500 million, its largest ever. It has invested over $1 billion into Anthropic in total, which makes its stake now worth nearly $22 billion at the IPO price.

Sound Ventures | Madonna's manager Guy Oseary and actor-turned-venture capitalist Ashton Kutchor invested around $35 million in Anthropic early on and put in another $400 million into the firm. The team, along with Sound Ventures' managing partner Effie Epstein, has a stake worth nearly $11 billion in the company.

Coatue Management | It has invested thrice in Anthropic. It made its first bet last year and then led or co-lead two major funding rounds for the company this year. It has invested a total of $4.75 billion in Anthropic, which includes $2.5 billion for the startup's funding round in February. Its stake would be worth $16 billion at the IPO price of $1.5 trillion.

GIC | The Singaporean sovereign wealth fund has invested over $4.5 billion in the AI firm after backing it in its past three funding rounds. Its stake is now worth around $15 billion.

Bessemer Venture Partners | It invested more than $800 million for around 0.5% ownership or around $7.5 billion at the current IPO price. This is over a ninefold increase from its initial investment, Bloomberg reported, citing sources.

Lightspeed Venture Partners | It first invested in Anthropic in 2024, earlier than most of its peers. It has invested a total of $3.5 billion into the company and plans to invest further in the IPO. Based on its investments in Anthropic's private financing, its stake is valued around $28 billion at the IPO price.

General Catalyst | The global investment company has backed Anthropic across various rounds beginning in 2025, investing around $2 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing sources. At the IPO price, the stake is now valued at over $10 billion.

Big Tech | The largest shareholders in Anthropic are its Big Tech backers. Amazon, Alphabet, Google and Microsoft all hold stakes in the company worth tens of billions of dollars post years of investing in as well as partnering with it. Anthropic also additionally arranged a $26 billion private placement for seven tech firms to invest more in the firm. Post, this, Amazon owns close to 15% of Anthropic's outstanding stock and Google owns about 14%. Both Google and Amazon's stakes are valued at over $100 billion.

Eric Schmidt | The former Google CEO was one of the first investors in Anthropic, backing the firm years prior any financial companies did. He is now set to be one of the largest individual windfalls from the public debut. He invested tens of millions of dollars in Anthropic in 2021 when it was valued at just $461 million, Bloomberg reported, citing PitchBook. At the present IPO price, Schmidt's stake is estimated to be worth around $15 billion.

data.title: Kraken parent Payward to acquire Tribe Capital to expand private-market offerings
data.description:
Kraken parent company Payward has signed an agreement to acquire Tribe Capital, a venture capital firm and asset manager with $2.7 billion in assets under management.

In a Wednesday statement, Payward said the deal will add private-market sourcing, underwriting, portfolio construction, and fund management capabilities to Payward's platform, expanding the range of investment products available across the company's client base.

Under the deal, Payward plans to develop new private-market offerings through Tribe's existing platform. Tribe is expected to operate within Payward's asset management business, according to the statement.

Tribe Capital, co-founded and chaired by Kraken Co-CEO Arjun Sethi, invests in early- and late-stage private companies across sectors including AI, advanced software, and financial infrastructure.

"Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe's investment approach to a global financial platform," Jonathan Hsu, co-founder of Tribe Capital, said in the statement. "We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward's infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities."

The acquisition is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions. The company did not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

The Block has reached out to Payward for further information.

Expanding offerings

Payward continues to expand its offerings through platforms including Kraken and xStocks. Last week, the company added more than 200 tokenized UK and European stocks through its xStocks framework, taking its number of tokenized assets past 1,500.

Payward also announced last week that it plans to introduce prediction markets for U.S. clients and offer equity perpetuals that run on its own exchange, clearinghouse, and broker.

In the third quarter of this year, the company reported $60 million in adjusted EBITDA, up from $23 million in the second quarter, but down 66% year over year, according to the private company's financial highlights released last week. Its total platform margin rose to $487 million in Q3 from $436 million in the previous quarter, but fell 12% year over year.

data.title: EU, Parliament agree to delay methane regulation by two years
data.description:
By Julia Payne

The EU and the European Parliament have agreed to delay by two years rules requiring ​oil, gas and coal importers to report methane emissions because of the disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran, the European Parliament said on Thursday.

The two-year delay is longer than the European Commission's proposal, made in October, for a one-year delay to the EU's ‌methane emissions rules for oil and gas imports, after pressure from governments including France and the United States.

The rules were due to take effect on January 1, 2027, but the co-legislators have agreed to a start date of January 1, 2029, according to the European Parliament statement.

Methane is the second-largest contributor to climate change, after carbon dioxide. It ⁠is ​far more potent than carbon dioxide, the biggest driver, ​over the short term and breaks down in the atmosphere much faster, so cutting it can have a rapid ​impact on limiting warming.

Earlier this month, the EU proposed staying with the Commission's one-year proposal but added a revision mechanism for two additional one-year delays if ⁠the Commission could not show implementation is ready. Parliament, however, had backed a three-year delay.

data.title: Australian employment falls sharply in October, jobless hits 4.9%
data.description:
Australian employment fell for a second straight month in October, while the jobless rate climbed to a fresh five-year high, a surprisingly soft result that bolstered the case interest rates have likely reached their peak.

Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed net employment fell 43,500 in October from September, when it dropped 36,400. Analysts had forecast a rise of around 25,000.

The jobless rate climbed to 4.9%, the highest since October 2021, from 4.7% a month ago. The participation rate dipped to 66.6%, while hours worked fell 0.2%.

data.title: Palm falls over 3% on weak rival oils, firmer crude caps decline
data.description:
Malaysian palm oil futures slipped more than 3% on Thursday, extending losses to a third consecutive session as weaker rival edible oils weighed on prices, though firmer crude oil capped the decline.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 139 ringgit, or 3.17%, to 4,247 ringgit ($1,032.83) a metric ton in early trade.

FUNDAMENTALS

  • Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 1.46%, while its palm oil contract shed 3.55%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were down 0.28%.

  • Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

  • Oil prices were steady after falling previously as increasing expectations for a supply surplus and higher interest rates softened sentiment, outweighing support from attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the lingering Iran war. O/R

  • Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

  • The ringgit , palm's currency of trade, strengthened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

  • Indonesia's palm oil exports, including refined products, totaled 3.92 million metric tons in September, according to data issued by the Indonesia Palm Oil Association.

  • Palm oil may test a support at 4,334 ringgit per metric ton, a break below could trigger a fall into the 4,204-4,276 ringgit range, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. TECH/C
